newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps flat - CFDs, mogas lose early gains - May 13.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps flat - CFDs, mogas lose early gains - May 13.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly flat on Tuesday after some markets slipped back from early gains.
Dealers said Asia was showing signs of weakness on gas oil and heavy fuel but the U.S. remained very strong on gasoline.
Brent crude CFDs were little changed after reversing early gains. Next week's dates ended at parity to July with the following two weeks at four cents and six cents under.
Earlier the 27-30 May week traded at flat with July.
Gasoline was little changed at $204 for June after losing an early $1 a tonne gain. July was $4.50 lower at $199.50 while August was pegged at 195.25.
Physical barges traded at $201.50 and $202.25 early but later at $201.
The third quarter crack spreads was slightly firmer with bids at $4.13 a barrel but the fourth was steady at at $3.10 .

Dealers were uncertain about what impact recent gasoline gains in the U.S. might have have. Some expected up to 300,000 tonnes to move across the Atlantic while others saw at least three cargoes of unsold German gasoline still looking for U.S. buyers.
Heavy fuel fell $1 a tonne with June barge swaps around $85 towards the close and July just 50 cents higher.
Dealers said the weakness reflected lower Rotterdam barges which traded between $84 and $85 amid poor bunker demand.
Jet premiums were little changed with June and July at $20 a tonne and $22 a tonne above the IPE respectively.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98).
